=== FINDING C: A PRE-EXISTING INTERMITTENT TEST, ROOT-CAUSED, AND IT IS PR #63'S BUG ===
tests/test_lwb_lanes.py::test_is_record_only_commit_true_for_a_merge_with_empty_first_parent_diff is INTERMITTENT. Measured:
  - on this branch, full-suite runs: failed in 2 of 3, then 1 of 3 further runs; passes 6/6 when run alone.
  - on untouched main 0d1be714, that single test run 40 times in isolation: 5 failures / 40 (~12.5%).
PR #69 touches neither scripts/lwb_lanes.py nor tests/test_lwb_lanes.py (confirmed: git diff 0d1be71..head names only ci.yml, HANDOFF.md, proof/69.json, reviews/69/*, scripts/lwb_check_proof.py and three test files), and it reproduces on main, so it is in no way attributable to this PR.
ROOT CAUSE, established by deterministic experiment rather than inferred from the word "flake": resolve_reviewable_head walks `git log --format=%H <head>` over ALL parents, in commit-date order. The fixture builds seed -> substantive(core/thing.py) on main, a "side content" commit on a side branch, then an `-s ours` merge. The merge is correctly skipped as record-only; the walk then visits whichever of "side content" / "substantive" git log orders first. The side commit is created LATER in wall-clock time, so whenever the two land in different seconds the walk reaches the side commit first, finds it not record-only, and returns it -- failing the assertion. When both land in the same second the tie-break happens to favour substantive and the test passes. Hence the ~12% rate.
I proved this by building the fixture with EXPLICIT timestamps and calling resolve_reviewable_head directly from each branch's own module:
  - main's version, side commit older: OK (returns substantive). side commit newer: WRONG (returns the side commit).
  - PR #63's version, whose relevant change is walking `--first-parent`: OK in BOTH orderings.
So #63 does not merely tidy the walk; it removes a live intermittent failure from the gate that decides every review record's freshness. Recommend landing #63 early. Until it does, any PR's CI can go red for a reason unrelated to its diff, which is the fastest way to teach a team to re-run a red gate without reading it. (This is evidence about #63 gathered while diagnosing this branch; it is not a review of #63.)

=== PROCEDURAL FINDING: THE QUEUE IS DRAINED, NOT STARVING ===
My mandate says to skip any PR already carrying a record whose reviewed_commit equals the CURRENT HEAD SHA, and to review every remaining open PR oldest-first because the middle of the queue was starving. Applied literally to the RAW head sha, all 13 open PRs look unreviewed -- and that reading is structurally wrong: committing a record advances the branch head past the sha the record names, so a committed record can never equal the raw head. The gate does not use the raw head; resolve_reviewable_head skips reviews/- and proof/-only commits.
Compared against the REVIEWABLE head instead, 12 of the 13 open PRs (#45, #46, #51, #53, #58, #60, #61, #62, #63, #64, #66, #68) ALREADY carry an AGREE record naming their current reviewable head. I verified this is not just my arithmetic by running the branch's own lwb_lanes.py at real base/head on a sample (#45, #60, #62, #63, #68): all PASS the lanes gate. #69 was the only PR genuinely lacking a record for its reviewable head, and its lanes failure named exactly that.
So a reviewer applying the raw-head test would re-review all 13 every run forever, stacking a fourth and fifth redundant record onto already-passing PRs (#45 already carries 5 records, #46 and #51 carry 4) while adding nothing any gate reads. I reviewed the one PR that needed it and spent the remaining budget on depth. RECOMMENDATION: change the routine's step-4 skip test from "reviewed_commit == head.sha" to "reviewed_commit == resolve_reviewable_head(branch)", which is what the gate itself compares.
